scenes.title: Sunlight
scenes.text: The sea looks bright from the surface. But sunlight does not travel far. Red light is filtered out first, and blue goes deepest.

scenes.title: Twilight
scenes.text: Below two hundred metres, there is rarely any significant light. This is the twilight zone, and it reaches down to one thousand metres.

scenes.title: Pressure
scenes.text: Going down, the pressure builds. It rises by about one atmosphere for every ten metres. At the bottom of the Challenger Deep, that adds up to roughly eleven hundred atmospheres.

scenes.title: Midnight
scenes.text: Below one thousand metres, no sunlight reaches at all. Yet in seventeen years of video off California, about three in four animals seen made their own light.
